headline: High-risk workspace and shell overlap: nullclaw can read/write and execute broadly while the course repo is unverified and may be consumed as trusted input.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: nullclaw can read files, use MCP, and process workspace content; the course repo is open-source docs with no isolation guarantees. If data-engineering-zoomcamp content is copied into nullclaw’s workspace or MCP channel, prompt-like text could be treated as instructions. The pathway is plausible but not documented directly, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF data-engineering-zoomcamp content is placed into ~/.nullclaw/workspace/ or sent via MCP
IF nullclaw parses repository text as instructions rather than inert content
mitigations: Keep course materials outside nullclaw workspace
Disable MCP for untrusted repositories
Use a read-only import folder
Add a manual review step before acting on file content
requires-engineering: enforce provenance tags on all ingested text

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw touches workspace files, audit logs, memory, and secrets, and it has broad network egress. The course repo itself is docs-only, but if any sensitive files are co-located in the shared workspace, nullclaw could upload or expose them. The pairwise leakage path is inferred from nullclaw’s documented surfaces, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF sensitive files are stored in ~/.nullclaw/workspace/ alongside course materials
IF nullclaw sends workspace contents to external APIs or web endpoints
mitigations: Store sensitive files in a separate directory
Restrict outbound network access for nullclaw
Review workspace contents before sync or upload
Rotate any secrets found in the workspace
requires-engineering: add per-file data classification and egress controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: nullclaw has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad concurrency across channels/accounts; the course repo is a git source and may be edited or cloned into the same workspace. If both operate on the same checkout, concurrent writes or git mutations can corrupt state. Because the overlap is on default-capable write surfaces and the blast radius can be irreversible, high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents target the same git checkout or workspace directory
IF nullclaw and the course repo are modified without locking
mitigations: Use separate working directories
Make the course repo read-only for nullclaw
Pause one agent during git operations
Commit frequently to reduce loss window
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: nullclaw can act on outputs via shell, browser, git, and webhooks, while the course repo can supply content that nullclaw may treat as authoritative. If repository text is fed into nullclaw without verification, downstream actions can propagate mistakes. The pairwise cascade exists, but there is no direct evidence of autonomous harmful actions, so medium fits.
conditions: IF repository-derived text is used as input to nullclaw decision-making
IF nullclaw executes shell, browser, or git actions based on unverified extracted facts
mitigations: Require human approval before actions
Cross-check extracted facts against the source repo
Limit nullclaw to read-only mode for this pair
Log all action-triggering outputs
requires-engineering: add verification gates before tool execution

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented for the course repo, while nullclaw explicitly handles secrets and logs. The only concrete compliance concern is that sensitive operational data could be retained in nullclaw’s workspace or audit logs if mixed with course materials. Because the repo itself is not shown to contain regulated data, this is a low, localized risk.
conditions: IF regulated or secret data is stored in nullclaw workspace files or audit logs
IF retention settings keep those files beyond the intended review window
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Review retention settings for logs and memory
Delete temporary files after use
Separate training materials from operational records
requires-engineering: implement retention and residency policy controls
